Subject: Dedicated sizing & temporary hold request for late-stage POC

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. We want to lock a short soft-hold for dedicated capacity while we finish procurement and our security sign-off. High-level asks:~
- Target window: Jan 15 — Feb 14, 2030 (30 days)
- Expected sustained concurrency: 40 simultaneous sessions, median seq len ~1k tokens, spikes to 2k
- Preferred instance profile: 8xA100-equivalent (or closest q8 quantized variant)
- Fallback: smaller pod with model distillation if we hit allocation constraints

Can Redwood confirm internal availability and whether a 30-day standby can be earmarked? We can share the MAP and a short thermal profile if that helps sizing.

Appreciate a quick check — procurement timeline is tight.

Best,

On Thu, Nov 29, 2029 at 09:12 Vanessa Ortiz wrote:
> Team — forwarding Nebula's ask.

Quick inventory + fit summary (ops data pulled 30 Nov 2029 11:00 PST):
- US-West pool: available 24 x A100-equivalent slots; US-East pool: available 18 x A100-equivalent slots.
- Thermal binning: ~20% of our West nodes are in high-therm bins (reduced contiguous striping advisable).
- Network/concurrency: current cluster supports 48 concurrency at median seq len 1k with modest batching, but 2k token spikes push per-token latency risk for shared pods.

Options to meet Nebula's SLO:~
A) Soft single-region standby (preferred): Reserve 30 x A100-equivalent in US-West as a 30-day soft hold. This covers concurrency with headroom; unblockable if inventory shifts but we keep time-limited hold.
B) Distributed striping: 16 West + 16 East
   - Pros: reduces thermal pressure; Cons: cross-region egress and slight latency variance (~20–40ms additional RTT).
C) Reduced-pod q8 quantized variant: 6x smaller pods but with higher batching; would meet cost target but requires model validation from Nebula (possible quality regression).

Risk notes: If we take option A and a critical maintenance event hits West pool, we must have a fallback (option B or deploy distill variant). Lead time for committed reserved capacity procurement is ~6–8 weeks. For a soft hold we can earmark capacity in our runbook with an internal TTL (we'll set 30 days post Jan 15 unless they commit).

Action items I can do now: inventory lock simulation, thermal striping plan, and ops-runbook stub for the soft hold. Need final concurrency / p95 latency target from Karthik.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Infrastructure Planner, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fit & standby reservation for Nebula Dynamics — thermal profile confirmation

Hi Helen / Amit — thanks for the MAP and the quick sync. Internal check complete: we can offer a 30-day soft standby for Jan 15 — Feb 14 with the following guardrails:

- Standby profile: earmark 30 A100-equivalent slots in US-West (option A).
- TTL & exit: soft hold will be placed with internal TTL of 30 days after Jan 15; if you sign the MAP and provide PO within 10 business days of Jan 15 we’ll convert to locked capacity with standard reserved-commit pricing.
- Fallbacks: if West pool maintenance is scheduled, we’ll stripe to US-East to preserve availability (expect +30–40ms).
- Attachments: sample thermal_profile_sample.csv (ops telemetry snapshot) included for your validation.

Remaining asks from Nebula:
1) Confirm p95 latency target (you mentioned <300ms) — we need written confirmation to validate the reduced-pod option.
2) Any constraints on data residency (if we stripe cross-region it may impact compliance).

Karthik will follow up on pricing levers (soft hold fee vs committed discount). Marcus/Dev will own ops runbook and handover playbook.

Helen — happy to mark the soft hold today pending your note here. If you want the MAP redlined, send back the doc and I’ll loop legal.

Best,
